common_name: Golden Diamond Pittosporum (Dwarf Golden-Yellow Foliage Mock Orange)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Golden Diamond tolerates salt spray and coastal conditions well, making it a common choice near the Gulf.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Golden Diamond tolerates coastal salt spray, wind, and poor soil better than many broadleaf evergreens, making it a reliable low hedge or foundation plant in Gulf Coast landscapes. This dwarf pittosporum forms a dense, mounding shrub of small, glossy leaves in a bright golden-yellow that holds its color best with a few hours of direct sun, providing season-long foliage color without relying on its inconspicuous, sweetly fragrant spring flowers. Its compact, naturally tidy habit needs little shearing to maintain shape, and it holds up well to both heat and the Gulf Coast's high humidity. Prune, if needed, right after the spring bloom to preserve next year's flowers, and expect a little more scorch risk in the hottest afternoon sun than green-leaved pittosporum cultivars.

common_name: Cream de Mint Pittosporum (Dwarf Compact Variegated Mock Orange)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Cream de Mint tolerates salt spray and coastal conditions well, making it a common choice near the Gulf.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Cream de Mint tolerates coastal salt spray, wind, and poor soil better than many broadleaf evergreens, making it a reliable low hedge or foundation plant in Gulf Coast landscapes. This dwarf pittosporum bears small, glossy leaves edged in creamy white surrounding a mint-green center, a soft variegated color combination on a naturally compact, mounding plant that stays smaller than the classic green-leaved species. Clusters of small, cream-white flowers appear in spring with the strong orange-blossom fragrance typical of the species. Its compact habit needs little shearing to maintain shape and holds up well to both heat and the Gulf Coast's high humidity. Prune, if needed, right after the spring bloom to preserve next year's flowers.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Marjorie Channon tolerates coastal salt spray, wind, and poor soil better than many broadleaf evergreens, making it a reliable screen or foundation plant in Gulf Coast landscapes. This larger-growing pittosporum bears glossy leaves boldly edged in a wide band of creamy white surrounding a gray-green center, a more dramatic variegation pattern and a larger mature size than compact cultivars like Wheeler's Dwarf, making it useful as a bright informal hedge or specimen shrub. Clusters of small, cream-white flowers appear in spring with the strong orange-blossom fragrance typical of the species. It holds up well to both heat and the Gulf Coast's high humidity; prune, if needed, right after the spring bloom to preserve next year's flowers.
